newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle trade brisk at $72, up $1 -trade.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle trade brisk at $72, up $1 -trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded briskly near midday Wednesday at $72.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week's top price, feedlot sources said.
About 25,000 head had sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklhaoma area by late Wednesday morning and 20,000 to 25,000 traded in Kansas, sources in those areas said.
Prices were lifted by continued tight supplies of finished cattle and firm demand from meat packers, sources said.
Tight supplies of finished cattle were attributed to a combination of light feedlot placements earlier this summer and active selling of fed cattle 20-30 days ahead of schedule, cattle feeders said.
The pulling ahead of marketings also was tied to increased profitability from lower feed costs and strong meat packer demand, they said.
A surge in wholesale beef prices to higher levels this week also lent support, sources said.
